introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné de 2 pages (page de garde et six questions sur une page), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food &Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » ; les points des sous-questions imprimés totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Pour 2(d), 3(a), 3(d), 4(c) et 5(a), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties (i) et (ii) imprimées (3+2, 2+3, 5+5, 4+4, 2+5).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au nombre exact d'éléments demandés (cinq, quatre, sept, huit...). D'autres réponses sont valables pour les questions de liste (types de repas, plats camerounais, équipements, signes de vieillissement de l'oeuf...) ; le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse, le sujet ne le détaille pas. La répartition des 10 points de 2(b) (2 par groupe) et de 6(a) (2,5 par équipement) est aussi une hypothèse.

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition : la liste des groupes de légumes (le sujet n'en impose aucune), les changements de l'oeuf qui vieillit (le sujet demande sept, d'autres manuels en donnent d'autres) et la température usuelle d'un congélateur (environ -18 degrés C). Aucune teneur nutritive ni durée de conservation chiffrée n'est avancée, sauf l'énergie d'un gramme de protéine (environ 17 kJ, valeur du programme).

Fautes d'impression du sujet recopiées telles quelles : « State five(5) reasons » (1a), « pastry making . » (1d), « first aid box . » (3a ii), « State five (5) qualities of a good waiter? » (4a), « importance of studying » au singulier après « five (5) » (3d ii, 5a ii), « vegetables salads » (2d ii), « left-over foods » (6b).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define the term first aid.

(2 marks)

(ii) List three items found in a first aid box .

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) First aid** is the immediate help or temporary treatment given to a person who is suddenly ill or injured, before a doctor or other qualified medical help arrives or before the person is taken to hospital. Its aims are to save life, to prevent the condition from becoming worse and to help recovery.

**(ii) Three items found in a first aid box (1 mark each).**

1. Bandages (and sterile gauze or dressings)
2. Adhesive plasters
3. Antiseptic (for example antiseptic lotion or cream)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Mention five (5) dietary recommendations for a healthy life style.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five dietary recommendations (1 mark each):

1. **Eat a balanced and varied diet,** with foods from all the food groups in the right proportions.
2. **Eat plenty of fruits and vegetables** every day for vitamins, minerals and fibre.
3. **Reduce the amount of fat, sugar and salt** in the diet (fried foods, sweets, sugary drinks and salty snacks).
4. **Eat fibre-rich foods** such as whole grains, beans and vegetables to help digestion and prevent constipation.
5. **Drink enough clean water** and avoid or limit alcohol, and keep to regular meals in moderate portions so as to keep a healthy body weight.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State five (5) aims of food preservation.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five aims of food preservation (1 mark each):

1. **To prevent spoilage** by destroying micro-organisms (bacteria, yeasts and moulds) or stopping their growth, and by stopping enzyme action.
2. **To make food keep longer** (to increase its shelf life).
3. **To make seasonal foods available all through the year,** including outside the season in which they are produced.
4. **To avoid waste of food and save money,** because a surplus can be kept for later use.
5. **To keep the food safe to eat** (to prevent food poisoning) and to keep its nutritive value, flavour and appearance as far as possible.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) List five (5) methods of preserving milk.

(5 marks)

(ii) Enumerate five (5) importance of studying food and nutrition.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Five methods of preserving milk (1 mark each).**

1. **Pasteurisation** - heating the milk to a moderately high temperature for a short time, then cooling it quickly, to kill harmful bacteria.
2. **Sterilisation** (including UHT treatment) - heating the milk to a higher temperature, so that nearly all bacteria are killed, and sealing it in bottles or packs.
3. **Refrigeration** - keeping the milk cold, which slows down the growth of bacteria.
4. **Drying** - removing the water to make milk powder.
5. **Evaporating or condensing and canning** - removing part of the water (with sugar added for condensed milk) and sealing the milk in tins.

**(ii) Five reasons why it is important to study food and nutrition (1 mark each).**

1. It teaches the **nutrients, their sources and their functions,** so that a person can choose a balanced diet.
2. It helps to **plan suitable meals** for people of different ages, activities and states of health.
3. It helps to **prevent diseases caused by poor feeding,** such as malnutrition, anaemia and obesity.
4. It teaches how to **buy, store, prepare and preserve food** hygienically, without waste and within a budget.
5. It prepares one for **careers and self-employment** (catering, hotel work, dietetics, food business).
